<ol><li><b>Avant de commencer</b>, repèr:
1. Before you start, spot the key, the time signature and the hardest passage.
  2. Keep the tempo: don't stop on a mistake.
  3. Read one note ahead.
<ol><li><b>Bats la pulsation</b> dès la:
1. Tap the beat from the very first listen.
  2. Write beat by beat: how many sounds in this beat? One (quarter note), two (eighth notes), four (sixteenths)…
  3. Check the total of each measure.

Measure replays a single measure: handy for tight rhythms.
<ol><li><b>Chante l'intervalle intérieur:
1. Sing the interval in your head before answering.
  2. Link each interval to the start of a song you know well (see "Tips for recognizing by ear" in the library).
  3. After answering, listen to the other intervals from the same note to compare.
<ol><li><b>Donne-toi la tonalité</b> ave:
1. Get the key in your ear with ▶ Scale and arpeggio, then the first note with ▶ 1st note.
  2. Keep the beat and don't stop on a mistake.
  3. Listen to the answer to check yourself, then sing it again.
<ol><li><b>Garde la pulsation dans ton c:
1. Keep the beat in your body (foot or head) while you tap.
  2. Count under your breath: "1 and 2 and" for eighth notes, "1 e & a" for sixteenth notes.
  3. Hold long notes for their full value; rests count just as much as notes.
  4. If a passage gets stuck, listen to the model, then try again without it.
<ol><li><b>Lis toute la question</b> : c:
1. Read the whole question: clef, key signature, "above" or "below"… one detail often changes the answer.
  2. Skip a hard question with the arrows and come back to it at the end.
  3. After the result, open each missed question: the right answer is shown, with a link to the topic.
<ol><li><b>Première écoute sans écrire</:
1. First listen without writing: find the beat and whether it's major or minor.
  2. Rhythm first, then pitches.
  3. Get your bearings from the tonic: leaps often land on notes of the tonic chord; the rest mostly moves by step.

▶ Scale and arpeggio puts the key in your ear; Measure replays a hard passage.
<ol><li><b>Trouve la première note</b> s:
1. Find the first note on the keyboard before you start.
  2. Think in intervals ("I go up a third") rather than note by note.
<ol><li><b>Écoute ▶ Tonalité</b> pour bi:
1. Listen to ▶ Key to really hear the tonic chord.
  2. Follow the bass: it's what reveals the degree (in C major: F → IV, G → V, A → vi).
  3. Listen for whether the chord is major or minor: that tells IV from ii, or I from vi.

After answering, listen to each chord again on its own.

• Start from landmark notes: in treble clef, the G on the 2nd line; in bass clef, the F on the 4th line. Find the other notes from there.
  • Aim for speed: naming a note in under a second is what makes sight-reading possible.
